text:
maria: Quick q — I'm coming back from an unpaid LOA on 2026-11-05. During the LOA I didn't accrue PTO. Do we prorate accruals for LOA months? Also I have 12 carryover days from last year. Does the 10-day carryover cap still apply or is there an LOA exception?
people-ops: Welcome back (almost)! :wave: Short answers: unpaid LOA >30 days pauses accruals; when you return accruals resume and are prorated for the remainder of the accrual period. The standard 10-day company carryover cap applies unless the LOA was protected leave that triggers a legal exception.
benefits: To expand: for parental/medical LOAs we evaluate statutory protections per country. If your LOA was unpaid but protected, we may grant an exception — we need the LOA paperwork in your file (case number or HR case link) to consider it.
payroll: Operational note: payroll treats LOA months as non-accrual by default. If you want excess days paid out instead of using carryover, we need manager approval before payroll cutoff for the month (Nov 25 cutoff for Dec payroll). Payout will appear on the next payrun and is taxable.
maria: Understood. Any quick example of how the math looks?
people-ops: Example (simple):
```
Annual accrual = 18 days
Accrual period = Jan 1 - Dec 31
Months worked before LOA = 8
Months worked after return = 3
Prorated accrual = 18 * ( (8+3) / 12 ) = 16.5 -> policy rounds to 16.5
```
people-ops: Carryover example: you have 12 carried days, company cap = 10 -> 2 excess. Options: (1) use the 2 before year-end (requires manager OK + coverage), (2) request payout for the 2 (payroll + manager approval before cutoff), or (3) apply for an LOA exception if your leave qualifies.
emma_mgr: I can cover the team rotation. If maria wants to take the 2 excess before the year-end shutdown (Dec 24-31), is that allowed?
people-ops: Shutdown window is a blackout for voluntary PTO. Exceptions are permitted only with manager sign-off + coverage plan + people-ops approval. For a returning LOA employee we are more flexible if coverage is confirmed. Please submit /pto-exception with: manager justification, coverage matrix, and LOA case ID.
payroll: Reminder: exception approval must be in place before Nov 25 payroll cutoff if you want to convert excess days to payout in Dec. If the exception is to take days off during the blackout instead of payout, approvals still need to be in place so schedulers can plan coverage.
maria: Thanks — I'll upload my LOA docs to HR case #HR-4567 and submit the /pto-exception form. Planning to use the 2 excess as days off before shutdown if approved.
people-ops-bot: Policy link: https://redwood.example.com/hr/pto-loa-proration-carryover — last updated 2026-08-15. Automated note: exceptions require manager + payroll sign-off.
people-ops: Sounds good. We'll triage after you submit the form and ping payroll if payout is requested. :white_check_mark:
maria: Great, thanks everyone!
